Data were acquired using a 3.0 T Siemens Skyra scanner at the University of Oregon's Robert and Beverly Lewis Center for Neuroimaging.

Blood oxygen-level dependent echo-planar images (BOLD-EPI) were acquired with a T2*-weighted gradient echo sequence (TR = 2000 ms, TE = 30 ms, flip angle = 90°, matrix size = 64 x 64, 33 contiguous axial slices with interleaved acquisition, field of view = 200 mm, slice thickness = 4 mm).

description.value: The reappraisal subscale of the Emotion Regulation Questionnaire for Children and Adolescents was administered to participants aged 10–17, and the reappraisal subscale of the Emotion Regulation Questionnaire was administered to participants aged 18–22. Scores were placed on a common 1–7 Likert scale and combined into a composite measure of self-reported emotion-reappraisal usage.

instructions.value: On Look trials, participants focused on the pictured food, imagined it was in front of them, and thought about consuming it. On Regulate trials, they focused on the food, imagined it was in front of them, and thought about the short- or long-term negative consequences of eating a large quantity. Participants used one selected reappraisal strategy on every Regulate trial and rated their desire honestly at the end of each trial.

stimuli.value: Images of low-energy-density foods (Neutral) and personally selected energy-dense foods categorized as Craved and Not Craved. Neutral foods included carrots, corn, cucumber, beans, broccoli, Brussels sprouts, eggplant, lettuce, squash, and tomatoes; energy-dense categories included chocolate, cookies, donuts, fries, ice cream, pasta, and pizza.
